ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Program Managers oversee the cost, schedule, and technical performance of acquisition, operations, and support activities, and are accountable for the overall success of the project or program.

They collaborate with others to plan programs across their life cycle, lead program teams and activities, and monitor the acquisition process to ensure that work efforts achieve the outcome specified in the Agency's business strategy.

They also validate and defend resource requirements, prepare procurement documentation, conduct technical evaluations, and monitor expenditures. They assess contractor performance and may perform source selection evaluation duties.

This position may be eligible for a RECRUITMENT INCENTIVE: selected candidates may be offered an incentive as part of the offer of employment. To receive the incentive, selected candidates must be eligible under 5 CFR Part 575, Subpart A, upon issuance of the Final Offer Letter.

Changes in federal employment status prior to issuance of the Final Offer Letter may affect eligibility. To receive the incentive, selected candidates will be required to sign a service agreement to stay within the position at NGA for the agreed upon time.

If the service agreement is terminated before its completion, the employee may be required to repay a pro rata share amount of the incentive to the government. Additional information regarding recruitment incentives for current federal employees can be found in DoDI 1400.25, Volume 2006.
MANDATORY QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: For this particular job, applicants must meet all competencies reflected under the Mandatory Qualification Criteria to include education (if required).

Online resumes must demonstrate qualification by providing specific examples and associated results, in response to the announcement's mandatory criteria specified in this vacancy announcement: Experience developing cost estimates, schedule, and performance standards pertaining to acquisition, operations, and/or support activities.

Experience with strategically planning future resource allocations and financial budgets to achieve program objectives. Experience with creating a stakeholder management plan to set and manage expectations on defined projects tasks. EDUCATION REQUIREMENT: A.

Education: Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Accounting, Business Administration, Engineering, Finance, Mathematics, Operations Research, Statistics, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), or degree that provided a minimum of 24 semester hours in one or more of the fields identified above and required the development or adaptation of applications, systems, or networks. -OR- B.

Combination of Education and Experience: A minimum of 24 semester (36 quarter) hours of coursework in any area listed in option A, plus experience in accounting, cost estimation, project management, requirements definition, or a related area that demonstrates the ability to successfully perform the duties associated with this work.

As a rule, every 30 semester (45 quarter) hours of coursework is equivalent to one year of experience. Candidates should show that their combination of education and experience totals 4 years. -OR- C.

Experience: A minimum of 4 years of experience in accounting, cost estimation, project management, requirements definition, or a related area that demonstrates the ability to successfully perform the duties associated with this work. -AND- Relevant Competencies: IT-related experience demonstrating each of the four competencies: Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Oral Communication, and Problem Solving. -AND- LICENSES/CERTIFICATIONS: DAWIA Certification may be required for this position; See Position License and Certification Requirements for additional details.

New Acquisition Workforce members or members transferring to a different or higher skill level will have, upon position entry, thirty-six months, forty-eight months, or sixty months, depending on the DAWIA Tier required, to achieve their certification.

Current Acquisition Workforce members must maintain their current certification by achieving 80 Continuous Learning hours every twenty-four months.

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: In addition to the mandatory qualifications, experience in the following is desired: Demonstrated proficiency in the processes that federal agencies use to acquire services and materials. Knowledge of fiscal law. Experience working with or supporting oversight organizations (i.e. ODNI, DoD, Congress).

Experience managing Artificial Intelligence programs.

Total Rewards of a Allied Health Professional The PCBH Deputy Program Manager serves as the professional leader of three PCBH teams at three locations and reports to the PCBH Program Manager. PCBH is co-located with the Primary Care medical teams, with an emphasis on integration of mental health services within primary care.

This responsibility requires broad-based clinical, administrative and supervisory knowledge and skills. Incumbent works closely and collaboratively with primary care medical teams within their designated clinic locations. Duties may include but are not limited to: 1.

As a full clinical member of the PCBH Team, incumbent conducts initial and comprehensive psychosocial assessments of Veterans referred by the Primary Care providers. They review all data, subjective and objective, and make a clinical assessment, identifying needs and strengths. Effectively uses professional skill, objectivity and insight.

Uses clinical training, insight and experience to interpret data and to identify viable treatment options. Assesses high risk factors, acuity and need for services.

Based on a comprehensive assessment, the incumbent uses professional judgment and advanced practical skills to make a clinical diagnosis and prognosis Treatment provided will be short term, problem focused and part of the care provided by the Patient Aligned Care Team (PACT). 2.

The PCBH Deputy Program Manager provides insightful assessment of cases involving mental health diagnoses, catastrophic medical conditions, dementia, and other high-risk diagnoses and determines if effective treatment can be provided with a short-term intervention or requires a longer term intervention.

Those cases requiring longer term treatment as determined by the incumbent will initially or later be referred to the BHIP or other specialty programs for such treatment (e.g. ADTP, PTSD, MHICM, etc.). 3.

Incumbent coordinates and provides mental health treatment for Veterans assigned to PACT; actively contributes to their PACT teams regarding goals, objectives and interventions for psychosocial and clinical treatment; and recommends adjustments to the Veterans treatment plans and interventions based on any changing needs and/or responses to interventions. 4.

Provides consultation services for primary care providers to maximize the effectiveness of their interventions in reducing health-risk behaviors and enhancing health-promoting behaviors, with a significant emphasis on a prevention-oriented model of care. 5.

The PCBH Deputy Program Manager may consult with other specialists in planning treatment for Veterans with co-morbidities. 6.Provides short term individual, family and group therapy services in accordance with the needs identified in the assessment and treatment plan. 7.Ultimately responsible for all entries in the Veteran's medical record (CPRS) and timely completion thereof, including discharge summaries and patient encounters. 8.Responsible for completion of all assigned clinical reminders for patients under their care, and performance measures assigned to the Care Line.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Education.

Have a doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

The specialty area of the degree must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed. For the purpose of meeting this requirement, the term "specialty area" refers to the specific specialty areas recognized by the accrediting body and not to specific job duties that might require special skills.

Currently, APA accredits doctoral programs in the specialty areas of clinical psychology, counseling psychology, school psychology, or combinations of two or more of those areas. PCSAS accredits doctoral programs in psychological clinical science.

CPA accredits doctoral programs in clinical psychology, counseling psychology, clinical neuropsychology, and school psychology. There are no job assignments in VHA that require the skills of a school psychologist; therefore, an applicant with a degree in the specialty area of school psychology is not eligible for appointment.

Strictly for the purpose of determining eligibility for appointment as a psychologist in VHA, there is no distinction between the specialty areas (with the exception of school psychology).

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re-specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re-specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: (a) The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA, or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and, (b) the specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

NOTE: The applicant must provide an official transcript and/or certificate documenting the completion of the re-specialization program, which includes completion of an APA or CPA internship. [Psychologists who have successfully completed a re-specialization program as described above and who were employed by the Department of Veterans Affairs prior to the implementation of this standard are considered to have fully met the educational requirements of these qualification standards.] [OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.] AND Internships (a) Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR (b) New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern, OR (c) VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96-151 (pre-1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR (d) Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) [OR (e) Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program.

NOTE: Psychologists who meet the requirements of this revision and who were employed by the Department of Veterans Affairs prior to the implementation of this standard are considered to have fully met the requirements of this qualification standard. Licensure.

Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia. English Language Proficiency. Social workers must be proficient in spoken and written English.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria).

Grade Determinations: Psychology Program Manager, GS-14 Experience: At least three years of experience as a professional psychologist, with at least one year equivalent to the GS-13 grade level.

Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate all of the following KSAs: Ability to organize work, set priorities, delegate tasks, and meet multiple deadlines.

Knowledge of and ability to utilize evidence-based practices and clinical practice guidelines appropriately and ability to guide staff in using these tools. Ability to deal effectively with individuals or groups representing widely divergent backgrounds, interests, and points of view.

Skill in managing and directing the work of others to accomplish program goals and objectives. Ability to translate management goals and objectives into well-coordinated and controlled work operations. Ability to establish and monitor production and performance priorities and standards.

Ability to analyze organizational and operational problems and to develop and implement solutions that result in sound operation of the program. Basic Requirements continued: under Education References: VA Handbook 5005/103, Part II Appendix G18The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-14.

Physical Requirements: In accordance with VA Directive and Handbook 5019 Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. If you like running stand-ups by the book, sending status updates, and waiting for someone else to make the hard calls, we're probably not your people. We look for PMs who ask "why" before "how", challenge specs that don't add up, and walk into a room full of ambiguity ready to create structure.

We're AI-native and we expect you to treat AI as a daily multiplier, not a gimmick. What we expect: ownership of your project end to end, straight talk with clients and the team, and the kind of curiosity that makes you actually care about what the device does, not just whether the sprint closes on time.

Be the single point of contact for our US-based clients: great communicator, diplomat, and when needed, negotiator
Manage web and mobile projects end to end: discovery, scoping, launch, and what comes after
Lead a cross-functional squad of designers, developers, QA, and other PMs
Run Scrum ceremonies, plan sprints, manage backlogs, timelines, budgets, and project health
Co-create product vision with clients: features, MVP strategy, the smartest way to deliver value
Lead staffing and resource planning with other chapters
Push for better ways of working, inside your squad and across the company
Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow, not as a party trick
How we work
Fully remote. We have a pet-friendly office in Warsaw and a coworking space in Gdansk if walls and coffee machines motivate you, but nobody will ask why you're not there. Working hours are flexible: most of the team operates between 10:00 and 18:00 CET, and that's when most meetings happen.

Evening calls with US-based clients (typically 16:00-20:00 CET, around 2-3 per week) are a normal part of the PM role here, always planned ahead. You'll be part of the PM chapter for knowledge-sharing, and at the same time leading your own project squad day to day.
What you'll get

s.h: 17,000-23,000 PLN/month net B2B, depending on your experience
s.t:
26 days of paid leave
10 days of paid sick leave
Saltus medical care
Self-development budget (2,000 PLN or 500 USD/year)

s.h: Truly flexible hours: you organize your day
s.t:
Fully remote, with pet-friendly Warsaw office + Gdansk cowork if you want them
All necessary equipment provided
Internal knowledge-sharing: tech talks, team sessions, library and conference budgets
Your first months
We aim to give you space to ramp up before owning a full project, but this is a real company with real deadlines: if a squad needs you sooner, we'll make sure you have the support to hit the ground running. You'll get paired with a buddy, meet the team, and start with real tasks while being guided by your team and leadership.

Monthly HR check-ins, real feedback after month two, and a proper review after month three: if things feel great on both sides, you're officially part of the crew. No one waits three months to tell you something isn't working: if it's great, you'll know; if something needs adjusting, you'll hear about it while there's still time to adjust.
Recruitment process
The entire process is in English. All interviews are recorded for internal evaluation purposes.
Application with a few screening questions
HR call, ~45 min, casual
Short take-home task (~60 min)
Technical meeting, ~90 min, with the Head of PM and COO
Final feedback within a few days
Once we're in touch, you'll hear from us fast. We don't ghost and we don't drag.
One more thing
intent is an equal opportunity employer. We care about what you can do, not where you come from. Send us your CV and a few words about why this caught your eye. Bonus points if you share a project you led that you're proud of, ideally one where the delivery was harder than the spec suggested.

s.h: About the role and what you will be doing
s.t:
The Senior Project Manager provides senior-level expertise to plan, organise, control, and deliver large, complex infrastructure and data centre migration projects across Ensono's client portfolio.

Operating within the Global Project and Implementation (GPI) practice, this role manages multiple company-wide initiatives simultaneously — from scope definition and budget planning through to delivery and post-implementation review.

A key part of this position involves building and maintaining strong relationships with client sponsors and internal leaders, including regular on-site engagement at the client's London office.

The Senior Project Manager interfaces directly with client executive management to understand critical business priorities and ensures every project is completed within agreed scope, quality, time, and cost constraints.

· Collaborate with stakeholders to ensure business requirements are clearly defined, understood, and documented

· Define project scope, risks, potential issues, and resource requirements at the outset of each engagement

· Ensure project benefits are realised while managing the impact of organisational change on the business and its clients

· Develop project phases and translate them into clear, measurable project plans

· Communicate internally and externally on delivery of work products, planning activities, and cross-organisational resource relationships

· Manage projects in full adherence to Ensono's project management methodology

· Manage project scope across mission, objectives, and requirements throughout the project lifecycle

· Manage project schedules, including key milestone dates and critical path tracking

· Lead the team in identifying project risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies; act as the primary escalation point and drive effective mitigation strategies to maintain project goals

· Provide leadership and strategic direction to the project team across all phases of delivery

· Oversee all project work streams, including timeline adherence, quality of deliverables, risk management, issue escalation, and stakeholder collaboration

· Work with all stakeholders to ensure governance frameworks and continuous improvement or transformation plans are established and maintained

· Establish deadlines, assign tasks, and monitor and summarise project progress for all relevant parties

· Develop business insights through analysis of results and communicate key findings to management to support data-driven decision-making

· Secure appropriate resources and personnel in collaboration with management to ensure projects are delivered on time and within budget

· Escalate barriers, risks, and issues that may impact timelines or deliverables in a timely and appropriate manner

· Manage the development of polished executive-level presentations and deliver findings to internal associates and external clients clearly and concisely

· Manage project status reporting in line with prescribed timelines for each engagement

· Develop measurement processes and methods to assess progress towards project goals and outcomes

· Manage project costs and budgets throughout the full delivery lifecycle

· Facilitate cross-training to support job rotation and minimise gaps in assignment coverage

· Provide coaching and constructive feedback to all project team members

· Mentor less experienced associates within the project management practice

· Interface with client executive management on-site at the client's London office to understand and address critical business issues and concerns

· Proficient in MS Office and MS Project

· Strong financial management skills, including experience with project budgeting and cost control

· Effective team management skills with the ability to lead matrixed, cross-functional teams

· Strong leadership and strategic direction capabilities

· IT outsourcing knowledge

· Strong infrastructure management experience

· ITIL and/or ITSM knowledge

· Ability to organise and define work in complex or ambiguous situations

· Ability to travel to the client's office in London as required

· Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment

· Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems (MIS), or equivalent experience

· Minimum of 7 years of complex IT programme and project management experience

· Demonstrated experience managing large-scale infrastructure and data centre migration projects

· MBA or Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, or Engineering preferred

· Project financial and revenue recognition experience preferred

s.h: 🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary
s.t:
As we enter a stage of rapid commercialisation and growth, we're looking for a Generation Flex Delivery Manager to own the successful onboarding of flexible generation and energy assets onto KrakenFlex across the EU.
This is a customer-facing delivery role with a strong technical bias. You'll manage an asset through the full onboarding journey, from initial discovery and technical analysis, through site design and gateway installation, to commissioning, testing and handover into live service.
You'll sit at the intersection of our customers, Electrical Engineering, Product and Customer Success Engineering teams. You'll need to understand both the connectivity and control architecture of our customers' assets and how those assets connect to and operate through the KrakenFlex SaaS platform .
You won't be expected to design the details of the integration solution or write the software yourself. Instead, you'll need enough technical depth across both areas to understand how they fit together, identify gaps and risks, challenge incomplete information and drive the right conversations to get a site successfully integrated.
Your role is to bring together three perspectives throughout onboarding:
Customer : What is the customer trying to achieve, and what do we need from them?
Product : How will the asset operate within KrakenFlex, and what product capabilities and configuration are required?
Engineering : How does the physical asset need to be integrated, connected and commissioned to make that solution work?
Your job is to make sure those three come together as one successfully delivered customer solution .
🚀 What you'll own
Own the end-to-end onboarding and delivery of Generation Flex assets BESS (grid-scale and C&I) and RES (Wind and Solar), from initial onboarding through analysis, site design, installation, configuration, commissioning, testing and handover into live service.
Build a strong understanding of the Generation Flex product and SaaS platform , including how assets are represented, configured, monitored and controlled within KrakenFlex.
Understand how the physical site and its electrical/control systems connect into the KrakenFlex software architecture, and bring those two worlds together throughout onboarding.
Work closely with Product and Software Engineering teams to understand the relevant GenFlex capabilities, product modules, configuration requirements and technical constraints for each customer and asset.
Translate between customer requirements, electrical engineering requirements and SaaS/product requirements , making sure each group understands what is needed from the others.
Understand the end-to-end data and control path from the physical asset through site controls, meters, PPCs, gateways and communications infrastructure into Kraken Flex, and from Kraken Flex back to the asset where control is required.
Ensure that the customer's intended use of the GenFlex product is reflected in the technical onboarding solution, including the required telemetry, controls, configuration, integrations and product modules.
Be able to explain to customers how their site will interact with KrakenFlex, both from a physical integration perspective and from a software/product perspective.
Work with Product teams to identify where customer or asset requirements do not fit current product capabilities, and ensure gaps, constraints or product dependencies are surfaced early.
Feed recurring onboarding challenges, customer requirements and technical integration pain points back into Product and Engineering teams to help improve and scale the GenFlex proposition.
Be the primary delivery point of contact for customers during site onboarding, setting clear expectations around what we need from them, what Kraken is delivering and what needs to happen next.
Work closely with our Electrical Engineering and Customer Success Engineering teams to ensure the technical information required to integrate a site is complete, accurate and available at the right stage of delivery.

s.h: Review and interpret customer technical documentation including
s.t:
Electrical Single Line Diagrams (SLDs)
Network and communications diagrams
Site and asset specifications
PPC and controller documentation
Modbus register maps
IP addressing and network information
Functional Design Specifications
Metering and telemetry information

Be confident discussing technical site architecture with customers and engineers, understanding how equipment such as generators, batteries, meters, PPCs, controllers, gateways and site networks fit together.
Identify missing, inconsistent or technically unclear customer information early and drive it to resolution before it becomes a delivery blocker.
Coordinate the preparation and review of Kraken integration documentation, including gateway architecture, communications diagrams, Kraken SLDs, integration designs and site configuration information.
Coordinate the Kraken Gateway delivery and installation process , ensuring prerequisites such as power, networking, connectivity and installation arrangements are understood and ready.
Manage readiness for key commissioning and testing activities, including:
Gateway installation and connectivity
Operational acceptance testing
Kraken market and service testing
Proactively manage delivery risks and communicate issues and mitigation plans clearly to internal and external stakeholders.
Surface blockers early and drive the right people together to resolve them rather than allowing issues to sit between teams.
Maintain clear visibility of the status and health of each site, including technical readiness, product readiness, customer actions, Kraken actions and upcoming milestones.
Continuously improve the Generation Flex onboarding process, identifying recurring technical, product or customer blockers and working with Engineering, Product and Operations teams to remove them.

* Shape HR policies and drive meaningful change across a complex organisation.
* Lead strategic HR projects in a dynamic and international environment.
## About Our Client ##
Our client is a large organisation based in Switzerland with an international and multicultural working environment
## Job Description ##
In this role, you will support the day-to-day management and improvement of HR policies, processes and practices.
You will review existing HR policies, procedures and guidelines and coordinate the necessary updates with HR colleagues and other internal stakeholders. This will involve working directly on documents, templates, forms and supporting materials to ensure they remain accurate, clear and easy to use.
You will help translate legal, regulatory and internal requirements into practical HR procedures.
You will follow relevant changes, identify which documents or processes need to be adapted and coordinate updates with the appropriate specialists.
A key part of the position will be process improvement.
You will review how existing HR processes work in practice, gather feedback from users, identify recurring issues and propose practical adjustments.
You will also use available data and KPIs to monitor processes and identify areas where efficiency or service quality can be improved.
You will work closely with different HR teams to support the implementation and consistent application of policies and procedures.
This may include answering questions, clarifying processes, preparing guidance and helping colleagues and managers understand how policies should be applied in practice.
You will coordinate a range of HR projects and improvement initiatives.
Your responsibilities will include preparing project plans, organising meetings and workshops, following up on actions, coordinating contributors, tracking deadlines and deliverables and ensuring that agreed changes are implemented.
You will organise and facilitate working sessions with relevant stakeholders to gather requirements, review existing practices and agree on practical solutions.
You will also support the rollout of new or updated HR policies and processes.
This includes coordinating validation, preparing implementation materials and working with communication colleagues to ensure that information is clear, accessible and available to the relevant audiences.
The position requires regular coordination with multiple stakeholders and the ability to manage several topics simultaneously while ensuring accurate follow-up and documentation.
## The Successful Applicant ##
We are looking for an experienced HR professional who enjoys working on concrete HR processes, policies and projects and who is comfortable moving between detailed documentation and stakeholder coordination.
You bring several years of HR experience, ideally within a large international organisation.
You have practical experience working with HR policies, procedures, process improvement and HR projects.
You hold a university degree or equivalent higher education qualification.
An additional HR qualification and familiarity with the Swiss employment and regulatory environment would be an advantage.
You are comfortable reviewing HR policies and procedures, understanding regulatory requirements and translating them into clear documentation and workable processes.
You have good project coordination skills and are used to managing actions, timelines, documentation and multiple stakeholders. You are comfortable organising meetings and workshops, following up on decisions and ensuring that agreed actions are completed.
You have a practical and solution-oriented approach.
You can identify gaps or inefficiencies in existing processes and suggest realistic improvements that make everyday HR activities simpler and more consistent.
Accuracy and attention to detail are important for this position.
You are comfortable working directly on policies, guidelines, templates, forms and process documentation and can ensure information remains consistent and up to date.
You communicate clearly and can work effectively with HR colleagues, managers and other internal stakeholders.
You are comfortable explaining processes, gathering feedback and coordinating different inputs to reach workable solutions.
Organised and autonomous, you can manage several activities at the same time, prioritise effectively and follow topics through to completion.
Fluency in French and English is required.
## What's on Offer ##
This is a varied and hands-on HR role where you will work directly on policies, processes, documentation and improvement projects.
You will have the opportunity to see the practical results of your work and contribute to making HR processes clearer and easier to use for employees, managers and HR teams.
You will join an international and collaborative working environment and interact with a broad range of HR specialists and internal stakeholders.
The position offers a good mix of operational HR work, project coordination and continuous improvement.
The organisation offers attractive employment conditions, flexibility, professional development opportunities and a supportive working environment.
The position is permanent and available at an 80-100% activity rate.
